priorQualification.scope: 8/8 actual ACIR experiment checks, synthetic canonical chain; no genuine proof/inclusion or atomic global-chain qualification

finding.sequence: page function including its final guard -> all contributor settle promises -> atomic staged coordinator commit -> committed notification -> return
finding.gap: A contributor can finish successfully after the page final canonical/account check while canonical or account context changes. Current successful-settlement path has no post-settlement revalidation. Existing contributor-rejection test proves rollback on rejection, not detection of a successfully settled changed context.
finding.evidenceStatus: Source-demonstrated ordering. A new pristine-versus-patched actual ACIR mutation regression is required before claiming runtime reproduction or repair.

recommendation.interface: Add optional captured beforeCommit: () => Promise<void> to existing OperationQueue.runSynced options and RunOperationArgs. Await it only after all original contributors settle, immediately before the unchanged stagedWriteCoordinator.commit.
recommendation.pageBinding: The pinned processRollingPreferencePage implementation constructs the hook internally from its immutable captured scope/network/class/artifact, queue anchor/header, selected canonical block/ordered compact root, detached receipt metadata and exact TxEffect bytes. Recheck existing canonical/network/class/header validation and original node receipt/effect agreement, then await the captured account contextGuard last. No caller-provided success boolean, no alternate receipt authority, no second ACIR execution.
recommendation.capture: Snapshot hook once before any await; reject malformed hook option. Page must always install a callable hook; a private per-operation closure can be populated after authenticated inputs are available, with a fixed failure if somehow unset. Legacy operations without hook retain existing behavior.
recommendation.failure: Hook failure enters existing drain/abort/discard path; no partial committed page and no completion/cursor update. Keep original settle and failure drainage semantics and original SerialQueue ownership through all work.
constraints: Hook performs read-only validation and must not re-enter the operation queue or start contributors.
Do not represent hook as a contributor: contributors settle concurrently.
Do not put RPC/network awaits in LMDB/IndexedDB atomic transaction or add another lifecycle.
Keep account callback authority separate from cryptographic chain validation; contextGuard cannot bless arbitrary chain state.
Reuse fixed sanitized page errors; no plaintext/receipt/error logs.

anchorAndPruning.validation: Page authenticates full ordered compact effects root against canonical header and matches selected transaction ordinal/hash/logs to exact effect. Original EventService recomputes commitment, requires it in effect nullifiers, rejects future-anchor data and stores canonical block hash/number plus tx/event order. Original NoteService requires note hash membership, stores block hash/number plus tx/note order, and queries nullifier tree at typed anchor hash.
anchorAndPruning.sameStores: PXE constructs one staged store array including noteStore and privateEventStore and supplies it to both StagedWriteCoordinator and BlockSynchronizer rollbackables.
anchorAndPruning.notes: NoteStore rollback removes every note created above prune floor and its contract/block indexes, and removes nullifier emissions above floor so earlier surviving notes regain their correct active status.
anchorAndPruning.events: PrivateEventStore rollback removes event rows above floor plus contract-selector and block-number indexes.
anchorAndPruning.atomicity: Installed reviewed block synchronizer resolves and checks conservative prune and configured-tier canonical headers before ONE transaction rolls back every store and updates anchor. Tips acknowledgment follows transaction; anchor update wipes contract sync and node caches. BaseStagingStore refuses rollback during open change set; queue serializes normal operations.
anchorAndPruning.limit: Source verification is not new runtime proof of orphan pruning for genuine preference balances. Existing synthetic note tests cannot establish historical private balance. New ACIR rows plus actual synchronizer rollback must cover both stores; subsequent genuine cold/reorg campaign remains required.

consumerPublication.existing: preference-reader captures network/rollup/board/class/account/schema in ROLLING_PREFERENCES_V1 AEAD scope; validates saved checkpoint against canonical number/hash before resuming authenticated prefix. Each decoded row has canonical block identity checks; full head/digest/marker checks precede completion.
consumerPublication.commitAndPublish: Reader rechecks trusted readiness, PXE anchor, private head and class before encrypted CAS and again after CAS before returning complete preferences. If reorg occurs during CAS, record may remain but nothing is published; next read rejects canonical checkpoint and rebuilds.
consumerPublication.integrationRequirement: New page method is NOT wired to this reader. Future bounded enumeration must retain these checks and official rollback before reading rows. A page admitted count is not authenticated full-history completion and cannot advance a consumer checkpoint on its own.

accountContext.capture: Session captures secret/salt/address, clones config, binds node/PXE/wallet provenance and original owner. Runtime guard binds exact selected account object and invalidated flag. Session uses per-wallet exclusive lock and busy lifetime.
accountContext.lastGuard: Move final account guard after all contributor and canonical validation awaits. A switch during settlement is then rejected before commit. No detached timeout or abort releases the lease while underlying work still runs.
accountContext.residual: A local invalidation AFTER the final guard while asynchronous KV commit is underway can still leave validated rows in the ORIGINAL scoped store. The proposed hook does not guarantee zero writes after such revocation. It never retargets storage to a new account. Session close rejects while busy, then waits for owned PXE queue on disposal.
accountContext.publication: Panel invalidation increments accountEpoch, aborts recovery and synchronously clears private RAM/DOM. After awaited readPreferences it checks epoch/unlocked account and abort before assigning preferences. Reader also guards every awaited boundary. Thus stale completion is suppressed by the consumer, not undone by pretending committed data never existed.
accountContext.requiredTest: Invalidate during contributor settlement: zero persistent rows. Separately invalidate during commit: test actual settled-write ownership, no cross-account result/DOM or completion publication, and explicit permitted old-scope retained rows. A stronger zero-write-after-revocation contract would require a separately reviewed synchronous epoch/transaction veto seam and native cross-adapter tests; do not imply current async guard provides it.

externalChainRace: No local transaction can atomically lock a remote canonical chain snapshot. A reorg after the last successful RPC may occur during or after commit. Committed rows remain block-bound provisional data; consumer canonical revalidation suppresses publication and subsequent official sync prunes orphan notes/events/nullifiers and invalidates derived checkpoint. The proposal eliminates the specific contributor-settlement window, not every time-of-check/time-of-use race.

installerExpansion.policy: Pin exact upstream and transformed hashes, transactional known-state apply/verify, reject mixed/unknown sources; temporary isolated copied SDK only until explicit deployment grant. Preserve exact copied compact verifier closure. No shared node_modules edits during experiment.

acceptanceBeforeIntegration: Pristine actual ACIR test: stage genuine encrypted head/event, contributor settles successfully after changing canonical block or account. Record existing commit outcome, then patched exact same fixture must reject and persist neither note nor event.
Hold contributor settlement: operation and exclusive queue remain pending; second operation cannot enter; release once only; reject changed context and drain every started contributor before abort.
Unchanged context commits one head and one event; hook runs exactly once after settle. Contributor rejection skips hook and preserves existing failure cleanup.
Canonical missing/changed header, class/network/receipt/effect mutation after successful settle rejects. Capture immutable inputs before await; no mutable callback replacement.
Late staged store failure rolls back all LMDB changes; existing normal operations without hook unchanged; malformed page hook fails closed.

Commit authenticated ACIR note/event, exercise installed actual BlockSynchronizer conservative reorg rollback, assert BOTH rows/indexes pruned and surviving earlier note/nullifier behavior; no balance qualification inferred.
Late chain change during KV commit is explicitly modeled: consumer publication rejects and subsequent sync prunes; do not assert impossible remote atomicity.

Later separately owned reader/panel tests cover canonical checkpoint invalidation and account epoch change during commit with no stale exposure; native browser IndexedDB and genuine proof/cold-recovery campaign remain separate gates.
execution: No tests, native execution, builds, services, source edits, dependency mutations or credential access in this design task.
